# UNIVERSE DESIGN

> A Moscow-based studio combining art, technology and innovation. We create media art
> installations that transform space, engage the viewer and open up new boundaries of
> perception. Our key specialization is volumetric LED screens and their non-standard
> use in art, advertising and event spaces.

The site is a portfolio. Every page has a plain-Markdown mirror at the same path with a
`.md` extension — prefer those over the HTML, which is media-heavy and carries almost no
text. The HTML pages render galleries and embedded video via JavaScript; the Markdown
mirrors list the same media as direct URLs.

## Studio

- [About the studio](https://universe-design.com/about.md): specialization, approach, capabilities
- [Home](https://universe-design.com/index.md): entry point and contacts

## Projects

- [All projects](https://universe-design.com/projects.md): index of the five main portfolio projects
- [ECHO 2.0](https://universe-design.com/projects/echo_2.0.md): media visuals built from GIF sequences and video for a volumetric LED installation
- [INTERVALS 2023](https://universe-design.com/projects/intervals2023.md): visual experience project showcasing digital art and motion design
- [LADA VESTA SW CROSS](https://universe-design.com/projects/lada_vesta.md): 3D automotive visualization, exterior and interior
- [PRE-EVENT OUTLINE 2025](https://universe-design.com/projects/pre_event_outline_2025.md): motion design and animations created for the event
- [FINOPOLIS 2022 | T1](https://universe-design.com/projects/t1_finopolis.md): event design for the financial forum, in collaboration with T1
- [UNIVERSE x LedPulse](https://universe-design.com/UNIVERSE%D1%85LedPulse.md): collaborative project on LED screen installations and media art

## Notes for agents

- The studio does not operate a public API, an MCP server, or any authenticated endpoint.
  There is intentionally no `/.well-known/api-catalog`, `/auth.md`, or OAuth metadata —
  those would describe services that do not exist.
- Crawling and training are permitted; see `/robots.txt` for the Content-Signal policy.
